A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdaDPSyn research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite reformatting and appendix expansion.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and information-extraction accuracies, clustering measurements, ablations, and membership-inference evaluations, including five-run results in Table 2.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds noise-parameter ablations, model comparisons, generation timings, and experiments at stronger privacy levels.

M1.justification: AdaDPSyn's token generation, radius refinement, coverage checks, and projected aggregation remain unchanged, as do the appendix algorithms. The revised experimental noise-parameter assignments and additional model evaluations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AGNews, DBPedia, TREC, MIT-G, and MIT-D with the same classification and information-extraction tasks. The added experiments vary models, hyperparameters, and privacy budgets within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: The comparison methods remain DP few-shot generation, instruction-only generation, noiseless generation, and randomly selected real demonstrations. The new model comparisons retain the comparator set used in the existing model experiment; the additional LLMs are evaluation configurations.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama-2-7B-chat, Gemma-7B, and Llama-2-13B configurations, a noise-parameter grid, MIT-G privacy budgets of 0.2, 0.3, and 0.5, and per-sample timing evaluation. It also reverses the documented σ1/σ2 assignments in retained experimental settings: for AGNews at ε = 4, v1 Table 12 gives σ1 = 3 and σ2 = 0.71, whereas v2 Table 13 gives σ1 = 0.71 and σ2 = 3. This establishes a reported settings revision, without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained shot-count, model, hyperparameter, and membership-inference studies, v2 adds σ0/σ2 sensitivity analysis, instruction-tuning and model-size comparisons, runtime analysis, and a detailed MIT-G real-versus-synthetic case study. Appendix C.13 also tests degradation under stronger privacy, substantially extending the robustness and diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Existing five-run mean-and-standard-deviation reporting and the membership-inference trial counts are retained; new Table 11 follows the same five-seed practice. However, the added model-comparison Tables 19–21 and low-ε Table 31 report only point estimates without accompanying run counts or dispersion, making uncertainty reporting less consistent across accuracy experiments.

E6.justification: Retained accuracy, clustering, and membership-inference results are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial numerical and qualitative evidence. For example, Table 20 reports DBPedia accuracy of 77.14% for AdaDPSyn versus 73.54% for DP few-shot generation using Gemma-7B at ε = 4. Table 31 adds MIT-G accuracies of 13.77%, 23.75%, and 30.56% at ε = 0.2, 0.3, and 0.5. New results also cover noise sensitivity, runtime, and generated-sample quality.

T1.justification: The definitions, privacy theorems, GoodRadius analysis, and RDP composition and subsampling proofs are retained. The added privacy-budget discussion in Appendix B supplies intuition and tuning guidance rather than new mathematical reasoning or guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same privacy and utility claims. The introduction adds a tentative contribution claim that the data-adaptive technique may apply beyond prompt synthesis and therefore has independent interest.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of privacy-budget allocation and noise-parameter stability, plus interpretations of the new model and timing results. Appendix C.13 newly discusses reduced detail, repetition, and missing exact genre labels in synthetic MIT-G examples as privacy strengthens. The existing limitation concerning absent theoretical utility guarantees remains.

D1.justification: v2 revises the documented noise-parameter assignments, adds practical allocation guidance in Appendix B, and supplies per-sample generation times in Table 22. Hardware, the approximate 24-hour reproduction estimate, prompt templates, and model/software access references remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work discussion are retained. Positioning relative to Tang et al., PATE, adaptive differential privacy, and private text generation remains unchanged; bibliography differences are formatting changes.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 adds explanatory passages and appendix subsections, removes the contents page, adds acknowledgments, and updates affiliations and some notation wording. These are localized structural and editorial changes rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The document is extensively retypeset, changing typography, margins, running headers, citation colors, and placement of tables and algorithms. Eight tables are added, including model and timing comparisons and MIT-G examples with colored genre annotations. Figure 1 and the existing displays are retained through relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful additional evidence about parameter sensitivity, model dependence, computational cost, and failure under stronger privacy. Revised noise-parameter documentation and allocation guidance also improve reproducibility. These are bounded improvements to an already supported study; several new comparisons lack uncertainty and run details, limiting the strength of their conclusions.
